First, note the date format given is DD-MM-YYYY: 01-07-1753 means 1 July 1753.  
Subtract 255 days:  
July has 31 days, so 255 days before 1 July 1753:  
Go back 30 days → 1 June 1753.  
Remaining 255 - 30 = 225 days to subtract further.  

June 1 back 31 days → 1 May 1753 (225 - 31 = 194 left).  
May 1 back 30 days → 1 April 1753 (194 - 30 = 164 left).  
April 1 back 31 days → 1 March 1753 (164 - 31 = 133 left).  
March 1 back 28 days (1753 not leap year) → 1 February 1753 (133 - 28 = 105 left).  
February 1 back 31 days → 1 January 1753 (105 - 31 = 74 left).  

Now from 1 Jan 1753 subtract 74 days:  
Go into previous year 1752 (leap year).  
Dec 1752 has 31 days: 1 Jan 1753 → 1 Dec 1752 is 31 days back (74 - 31 = 43 left).  
Nov 1752 has 30 days: 1 Dec 1752 → 1 Nov 1752 is 30 days back (43 - 30 = 13 left).  
From 1 Nov 1752 subtract 13 days → 19 Oct 1752.  

FINAL_ANSWER: 1752-10-19
